body_html:
Spanish capitalization rules surprise learners, because Spanish uses far fewer capital letters. Days of the week, months, languages, nationalities, religions and even titles like señor are written in lower case: el lunes 3 de marzo, hablo inglés, es mexicana. Book and movie titles capitalize only the first word. Copying English capitalization into Spanish is one of the clearest signs of a translated text. Here’s what to capitalize and what to leave alone.

Key takeaways
  • Lower case: days, months, seasons, languages, nationalities, religions, and yo.
  • Titles of books, movies and songs: only the first word and proper nouns: Cien años de soledad.
  • Usted, señor, doctor are lower case in full; abbreviations are capitalized: Ud., Sr., Dr.
  • Capital letters keep their accents: Álvaro, ÉXITO.
{{toc}}

Spanish capitalization rules: lower case words

CategoryEnglishSpanish
DaysMondaylunes
MonthsJanuaryenero
SeasonsSpringprimavera
LanguagesEnglish, Spanishinglés, español
NationalitiesMexicanmexicano
Religions and their followersCatholic, Buddhistcatólico, budista
“I”Iyo
Cardinal pointsNorthnorte (unless part of a name: Corea del Norte)

The RAE’s Diccionario panhispánico de dudas sets out these rules, together with the cases where capitals are needed.

What Spanish does capitalize

  • The first word of a sentence and after a period, question or exclamation mark that closes a sentence.
  • Proper names of people, places and institutions: María, Lima, la Universidad de Salamanca.
  • Names of holidays and historical periods: Navidad, Semana Santa, la Edad Media.
  • Abbreviations of titles: Sr., Sra., Dr., Ud.
  • Names of deities: Dios, Alá.

Titles of books, movies and songs

Spanish capitalizes only the first word and any proper nouns in titles of creative works:

  • Cien años de soledad (not Cien Años de Soledad)
  • La casa de papel
  • El amor en los tiempos del cólera

Names of newspapers and magazines are an exception and capitalize all main words: El País, La Nación.

{{image:2}}

Titles and forms of address

When written in full, titles and positions are lower case: el señor García, la doctora Ruiz, el rey Felipe, el papa Francisco, la presidenta. Abbreviated, they take a capital: el Sr. García, la Dra. Ruiz. Likewise usted in full, Ud. or Vd. abbreviated. See {{link:tu-vs-usted|tú vs usted}}.

{{book:a-road-in-bloom}}

Capitals keep their accents

A persistent myth says capital letters don’t need accents. The RAE is clear that they do: Ángela, ÁFRICA, Él lo sabe. Omitting them was once a limitation of typewriters, not a rule. More in {{link:spanish-accent-marks|Spanish accent marks}}.

After a colon

After a colon, Spanish normally continues in lower case: Tengo tres hermanos: dos chicos y una chica. Capitals are used after the greeting in letters (Querida Ana: Te escribo para…) and when quoting a full sentence. See {{link:spanish-punctuation-rules|Spanish punctuation rules}}.

Why this happens

English capitalizes many categories of words for reasons of tradition: days, months, languages and the pronoun “I”. Spanish treats them as common nouns and adjectives. When learners write El Lunes hablo con mi profesor de Español, every capital is wrong except the first. Translation software sometimes makes the same mistake, which is why I always check capitals carefully when reviewing machine-translated Spanish. Software interfaces and marketing copy are full of title-case headings copied from English; in Spanish, sentence case is the norm.

Headlines and headings

English often uses title case in headings (“How to Learn Spanish Fast”). Spanish uses sentence case: Cómo aprender español rápido. Websites, presentations and documents in Spanish should follow this, even if the English original didn’t.

Regional and institutional names

Geographical names capitalize only the proper part: el río Amazonas, la cordillera de los Andes, el mar Mediterráneo. But when the common noun is part of the official name, it takes a capital too: Río de la Plata, Ciudad de México. Institutions, organizations and companies capitalize their main words: el Ministerio de Educación, el Instituto Cervantes. Subjects of study are lower case in general (estudio historia) but capitalized as official course or degree names (Grado en Historia del Arte).

Try it yourself

Correct the capitals: El Martes 12 de Octubre, la Señora Gómez habló en Francés sobre su libro “El Jardín Secreto”.

Answer: El martes 12 de octubre, la señora Gómez habló en francés sobre su libro El jardín secreto.

All mistake types in {{link:common-spanish-mistakes|my guide to common Spanish mistakes}}.

{{quiz}}

Final thoughts

When in doubt, Spanish uses lower case. Keep capitals for sentence starts, proper names, holidays, abbreviations and the first word of titles, and keep the accents on capitals. Your Spanish will look native, not translated.

faq.q: Are days and months capitalized in Spanish?
faq.a: No. Days, months and seasons are written in lower case: el lunes, enero, primavera.

faq.q: Are languages and nationalities capitalized in Spanish?
faq.a: No: hablo español, es mexicana. Only proper names of countries take capitals: México.

faq.q: How are book titles capitalized in Spanish?
faq.a: Only the first word and proper nouns: Cien años de soledad. Newspapers are an exception: El País.

questions.explain: Days and months are lower case.
Only the first word is capitalized.
The RAE requires accents on capitals: Ángel.
Abbreviations are capitalized; full titles are lower case.
